description: The President's opening address, authored to the shape of real inaugural and state-of-the-union addresses (an opening, a story of the country, named priorities each tied to a law, a close) and written for this game's Presidents: every law and priority is a slot or a required fact read from the world's records, and the address says no figure at all (owner, Oct 27: "none of that real data in there"; Nov 1: "I don't like where this part of the speech where it just laces statistics"). Each sentence has a polished and a plain version for the speaker's recorded manner. No real President's words.

slots.about: the policy question's spoken noun phrase
slots.to: the policy question's spoken verb phrase
slots.state-name: the player's state, whose law the laws engine reads
slots.place: a state the President campaigned in
slots.name: a governor on the stage
slots.vice-president: the Vice President's name, from the officials engine's seat; said with the seat's title at first mention and by role after (said-as)
slots.speaker: the Speaker of the House's name, from the officials engine's presiding seat; said with the seat's title at first mention and by role after (said-as)
slots.hardest: the year's subject that moved furthest the wrong way, in the bank's subject words, from the macro months and the term read
slots.best: the year's subject that moved furthest the right way, in the bank's subject words, from the macro months and the term read
slots.first-about: the President's first priority as a noun phrase, from their recorded stance and the laws engine's row
slots.first-to: the President's first priority as a verb phrase, from the same records
slots.change-unemployment: how far unemployment moved over the year, in the bank's change words, from the macro months or the term read
slots.change-inflation: how far inflation moved over the year, in the bank's change words, from the macro months or the term read
slots.change-growth: how far growth moved over the year, in the bank's change words, from the macro months or the term read
slots.change-wages: how far wages moved over the year, in the bank's change words, from the macro months or the term read
slots.change-mortgage: how far mortgage moved over the year, in the bank's change words, from the macro months or the term read

slots.change-rent: how far rent moved over the year, in the bank's change words, from the macro months or the term read
slots.change-crime: how far crime moved over the year, in the bank's change words, from the macro months or the term read
slots.change-schools: how far schools moved over the year, in the bank's change words, from the macro months or the term read
slots.change-health: how far health moved over the year, in the bank's change words, from the macro months or the term read
slots.change-roads: how far roads moved over the year, in the bank's change words, from the macro months or the term read
slots.change-environment: how far environment moved over the year, in the bank's change words, from the macro months or the term read
slots.say-unemployment: unemployment in the bank's subject words, when the year holds a claim on it
slots.say-inflation: inflation in the bank's subject words, when the year holds a claim on it
slots.say-growth: growth in the bank's subject words, when the year holds a claim on it

slots.say-health: health in the bank's subject words, when the year holds a claim on it
slots.say-roads: roads in the bank's subject words, when the year holds a claim on it
slots.say-environment: environment in the bank's subject words, when the year holds a claim on it
slots.context-years: how many whole years a context sentence covers: the macro engine's months, or the years since the speaker took office for an area of the term read
slots.context-amount: a measure's average over the context's years, to one decimal, from the macro engine's months
slots.vice-president-addressed: the Vice President spoken to, said with title and name every time
slots.vice-president-object: the Vice President where the sentence needs the object case (with her)
slots.vice-president-possessive: the Vice President where the sentence needs the possessive (her counsel)
slots.side: the question as the speaker's side says it (question-names.json `for` or `against`)
slots.speaker-object: the Speaker where the sentence needs the object case
slots.speaker-possessive: the Speaker where the sentence needs the possessive
slots.today: how the policy question stands today, by the law in force and as the speaker's side describes it (question-names.json `today`)
slots.first-side: the speech's first point as the speaker's side says it (question-names `for` or `against`), for the close
slots.today-clause: the same sentence as `today`, in the case it takes after an opener and a comma
slots.belief: what the speaker believes, a clause worded from the belief-words pieces by the question's family and the speaker's pole of it
slots.today-question: the same sentence as `today-clause` without its period, said inside a question to the audience
slots.today-clause-second: `today-second` after an opener and a comma
slots.today-clause-third: `today-third` after an opener and a comma
slots.today-question-second: `today-second` inside a question to the audience
slots.today-question-third: `today-third` inside a question to the audience
slots.law-name: the law in force on the question, as the thing itself (question-names.json `law`: "paid family leave", "the higher federal minimum wage")
slots.realm-name: the governor's state or the mayor's town by name, from the speaker's jurisdiction record
slots.theme-name: the speech's one theme said as people say it (speech-outlines.json `themeNames`, by the question family)
slots.body: the local body the speaker speaks to or sits on, as people say it, from the office row's body name
slots.office-title: the local office the speaker holds or seeks, as people say it, from the office row's title or the presiding post
slots.presiding: whoever presides over the body, by the post's title and family name (said-as, addressed)
slots.condition-law: a law of the speaker's jurisdiction that took effect in the past year, by its spoken name (the laws engine's row)
slots.condition-disaster: a disaster declared for the place in the past year, by its kind (the disasters engine's declaration)
slots.budget-year: the fiscal year of the budget the speaker's government lives under (the budgets engine's row)
slots.budget-gap: how far the speaker's government's budget runs ahead or short, as people say a sum ("about $40,000", "about $2.3 billion"), from the budgets engine's row: what it takes in against what it spends
slots.condition-law-reached: the law-reach records show the law of condition-law has reached people here (law-reach host.ts reachedBy); said only as the sentence's tie, never as a figure
slots.measure: what the body the speech is given to passes, as it names its measures (bill, ordinance)
slots.first-after: how the first ask's question will stand once the ask passes, in the speaker's side's words, where it changes the law
slots.first-reason: the first ask's own reason on the speaker's side, where the belief has not said it
slots.theme-short: the theme said short for a close (speech-outlines.json themeShort)
slots.speaker-addressed: the Speaker of the House spoken to, with title and name
slots.body-name: the body a local speaker addresses, by the name its record gives it, said as to its face ('the Groton Select Board'), from the office record
slots.condition-measure: a hurt address's worst condition: the area's measure that moved furthest the wrong way, in its measure words (area-names.json), from the term read
slots.condition-change: how far that measure moved since the speaker took office, through the count-words reader (changeSaid), from the term read's two web rows
slots.turn-to: the speech's theme by its spoken name, where a hurt address turns from its answer to the theme
slots.realm-bare: the governor's state or the mayor's town by name, from the speaker's jurisdiction record
slots.context-name: The measure said short, from the speaker's record.
slots.good-name: The measure the term improved, said short, from the term's own record.
slots.belief-sentence: What the speaker believes on the question, as a sentence of its own, from the bank's belief clause.
